title: Rule on Penalty, Interest and Fees — Benefit Overpayment Accounts
content:
This rule governs the fraud penalty, interest and the returned-payment fee on Benefit Overpayment Accounts.

**(1) Penalty.** A fraud overpayment carries a penalty of the classification's penalty share of the principal, assessed once at establishment, rounded to the cent, and credited to the Unemployment Trust Fund when collected. The penalty is never waived.

**(2) Interest.** Interest accrues only on fraud overpayments, as simple interest at the classification's monthly rate on the unpaid principal at the end of each calendar month. It never accrues on penalty, interest or fees. The month's interest is the monthly rate multiplied by the unpaid principal, rounded to the cent.

**(3) Unpaid principal.** The unpaid principal is the principal assessed, less the principal applied by repayments, offsets, intercepts and waiver, cancellation and write-off adjustments, plus the principal reversed by returned repayments and refunds.

**(4) First interest month.** The first interest month is the calendar month that begins after the interest start days following the determination date.

**(5) Once per month.** Interest is booked once per overpayment per accrual month. The Department's ledger for that overpayment is the record checked before a month's interest is booked; a month that already carries an interest entry on that overpayment is not booked again.

**(6) Plans and appeals.** For a first-offense fraud overpayment no interest accrues for a month in which the repayment plan was current for the whole month; a repeat-offense fraud overpayment accrues interest whether or not a plan is current. No interest accrues for a month in which the overpayment was suspended for appeal.

**(7) Returned repayments — no longer in force.** The clause "A repayment returned unpaid by the bank reverses its application and is followed by the returned-payment fee, which is booked as its own fee component." is no longer in force. It has been superseded by the Department's current basis for the returned-payment fee owed when a repayment is returned unpaid.

## Worked figures (hypothetical)

- *Hypothetical:* a fraud overpayment with a determination date of 20 January and 30 interest start days. Thirty days after 20 January is 19 February; the calendar month that begins after that is March, so March is the first interest month.
- *Hypothetical:* at the end of a month the unpaid principal is USD 1,234.56 and the monthly rate is 1 percent. The month's interest is USD 12.3456, rounded to USD 12.35.
- *Hypothetical:* a first-offense fraud overpayment whose plan was current from the 1st to the last day of April accrues no interest for April; had the plan been current for only part of April, interest for April would accrue. A repeat-offense fraud overpayment accrues for April either way.

superseded_clauses: A repayment returned unpaid by the bank reverses its application and is followed by the returned-payment fee, which is booked as its own fee component.
